articles.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Could Bayern sign Haaland to replace Kane?
articles.description: Erling Haaland is contracted to Manchester City for another eight years, but could Bayern Munich sign him? Transfer Talk has the latest.
articles.headlineJa: 移籍の噂・最新ニュース：バイエルンはケインの後釜としてハーランドを獲得するのか？
articles.descriptionJa: アーリング・ハーランドはマンチェスター・シティとさらに8年間の契約を結んでいますが、バイエルン・ミュンヘンが彼を獲得する可能性はあるのでしょうか？「Transfer Talk」が最新情報をお届けします。
articles.body:
Erling Haaland is contracted to Manchester City for another eight years, but could Bayern Munich sign him? Plus, Manchester United have identified a new potential replacement for left back Luke Shaw.

Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Bayern Munich have emerged as suitors for Manchester City striker Erling Haaland, according to TEAMtalk. The Bundesliga side are believed to see the 26-year-old as a potential future replacement for Harry Kane, who they want to remain at the Allianz Arena for a further two years before assessing whether a move for Haaland is possible. Meanwhile, TEAMtalk reports that Vincent Kompany's side are also keen on Nottingham Forest attacking midfielder Morgan Gibbs-White, and could be contenders for his signature next summer amid plans to add him to their squad with England compatriot Kane.

- Liverpool and Manchester United are interested in Crystal Palace defender Tyrick Mitchell, TEAMtalk reports. The Red Devils reportedly see the 27-year-old as an alternative to Newcastle's Lewis Hall as they continue plans to identify a long-term successor to Luke Shaw. Mitchell entered the final 12 months of his contract in the summer, and it is said that Chelsea are also monitoring his situation, attracted to the opportunity of landing him on a free transfer.

- Chelsea and Manchester City are exploring a move for AC Milan forward Francesco Camarda, according to TEAMtalk. The Blues are said to have tracked the 19-year-old for some time, and they are monitoring whether an opportunity to land him could arise due to a lack of minutes for the Rossoneri since returning from his loan spell at Lecce. Camarda scored one goal in 21 Serie A appearances last season.

- Napoli are struggling to make progress in talks with the representatives of midfielder Kevin De Bruyne over a new contract, transfer journalist Nicolo Schira reports. Discussions have reportedly stalled with the 35-year-old, who arrived at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona on a two-year deal in the summer of 2025, and it is now said that they are "on the verge" of parting ways next summer. De Bruyne was previously linked with clubs in Major League Soccer and the Saudi Pro League before deciding to join Gli Azzurri.

- On-loan Aston Villa winger Alejandro Garnacho is attracting interest from clubs in LaLiga, the Daily Mail reports. The 22-year-old is believed to be on the radar of several clubs in Spain amid struggles to earn a place in Unai Emery's side, with 32 minutes of action in the Premier League spread across three substitute appearances. He is on loan from Chelsea, but any potential permanent move at Villa Park would require conditions to be met, which would see a £43 million proposed deal become official.

Other rumors

- Liverpool have no plans to consider parting ways with attacking midfielder Florian Wirtz despite reports of interest from Bayern Munich.

articles.headline: Andy Robertson opens up about Liverpool after Diogo Jota's death: 'We didn't care about football'
articles.description: Former Liverpool defender Andy Robertson has said that the death of teammate Diogo Jota was "horrendous" and had a major impact on the players that knew him.
articles.headlineJa: アンディ・ロバートソン、ディオゴ・ジョタの死後のリヴァプールについて語る：「サッカーのことなど頭になかった」
articles.descriptionJa: 元リヴァプールのDFアンディ・ロバートソンは、チームメイトであったディオゴ・ジョタの死は「恐ろしいこと」であり、彼を知る選手たちに甚大な影響を与えたと語った。
articles.body:
Former Liverpool defender Andy Robertson has said that the death of teammate Diogo Jota in 2025 was "horrendous" and had a major impact on the players that knew him.

Speaking on The Overlap, the Scotland international expressed empathy for the new signings who joined Liverpool last summer -- among them were Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz -- as he stated that the club was "heartbroken" and the new arrivals struggled to settle in.

Robertson also said that Jota's death definitely had an impact on the team's performances, as players came to terms with the loss of one of their friends.

Liverpool finished fifth last season and head coach Arne Slot was sacked in the summer.

"It's difficult to describe or talk about. What we went through was horrendous," he said.

"The new signings, they're coming into a club that was heartbroken. I felt so sorry for these guys because they'd signed, and they'd signed for big money, and it took them months to settle in. We didn't care about football.

"That was the truth of it, we didn't care about football because we'd just lost one of our best mates in the changing room.

"All footballers have that edge and, when you lose that edge sometimes, you can't perform to your best. I think last season we lost the edge.

"When I look back on it now, I think we lost that determination a little bit because at times we were maybe thinking 'what's the point? Look at what Jota's family is going through, I mean look at his kids...'"

Robertson also said that Jota was the friend of his Liverpool teammates, not just a footballer.

"We were grieving. He was our mate at the end of the day, he wasn't a footballer to us. He was a teammate, a friend. For us, it was incredibly difficult.

"The week before he died, I was at his wedding. That's one of the most difficult things you'll ever go through, seeing him on the happiest day of his life and then the next week, you're seeing his family torn apart."

Asked if he felt that he was able to grieve or if he felt like he just had to go straight back to being a footballer, Robertson praised Slot and said that the players felt they could speak to one another about what had happened.

- Trent Alexander-Arnold found 'closure' at Anfield after Diogo Jota's death

"We spoke a lot. The manager was really good to be fair. Our pre-season was barely anything because Arne said: 'If you don't want to train, you don't train.' And that was his attitude of the pre-season," he said.

"We had a psychologist that worked at the club anyway and he set up little groups where you could grab a coffee and talk. We did that quite a few times and I think that helped.

"It was incredibly difficult for us but we just couldn't help feel sorry for his family, for his wife. Their life got flipped completely upside down ...We managed to get through it together, we just said that we'll always remember him.

"But we had to play football at the end

articles.headline: Clippers name Trent Redden interim president of basketball ops
articles.description: The LA Clippers named general manager Trent Redden as the team's interim president of basketball operations while Lawrence Frank serves his six-month suspension.
articles.headlineJa: クリッパーズ、トレント・レデンをバスケットボール部門の暫定代表に任命
articles.descriptionJa: ロサンゼルス・クリッパーズは、ローレンス・フランクが6か月間の停職処分を受ける中、ゼネラルマネージャーのトレント・レデンをチームのバスケットボール部門暫定代表に任命した。
articles.body:
The LA Clippers named general manager Trent Redden as the team's interim president of basketball operations while Lawrence Frank serves his six-month suspension stemming from the NBA's investigation into salary cap circumvention.

The announcement was made via a video message from interim team governor and CEO John Gibson to fans. Gibson, who is serving as interim governor while Steve Ballmer serves his one-year suspension, also announced that assistant general manager Mark Hughes will take over GM duties in the meantime.

 

Redden joined the Clippers' front office in 2017 after a long run with the Cleveland Cavaliers. He was promoted from assistant general manager to GM in 2023. Hughes also came to the Clippers in 2017 after several years as an assistant coach in the NBA after his pro playing career.

The suspensions of Ballmer and Frank came down after a yearlong investigation into the Clippers by law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz. Along with Ballmer's suspension, the NBA issued a $30 million fine and the forfeiture of five first-round draft picks.

Ballmer recently accepted the NBA's punishment, saying in a statement, in part, that though there are still disagreements with the findings, "We are complying with the penalties assessed by the league, have paid the fine and are moving forward."

articles.headline: Woman says she reported alleged 49ers impersonator to team in December
articles.description: A woman who says she is a victim in the FBI's fraud case against Daejon Love said she sent a "complaint/concern" to the Niners in December 2025, eight months before Love was arrested and charged with wire fraud and conspiracy to commit wire fraud.
articles.headlineJa: 49ers関係者を装ったとされる人物について、女性が12月にチームに通報したと語る
articles.descriptionJa: デイジョン・ラブに対するFBIの詐欺事件の被害者であると主張する女性は、ラブが電信詐欺および電信詐欺の共謀罪で逮捕・起訴される8か月前の2025年12月に、49ersに「苦情・懸念」を送ったと述べた。
articles.body:
A woman who says she is a victim in the FBI's fraud case against Daejon Love, a man who is accused of impersonating a San Francisco 49ers player, told ESPN on Tuesday that she submitted a complaint about him via the team's website in December, eight months before he was arrested.

Gwen Herndon said she sent a "complaint/concern" form submission to the Niners on Dec. 20, 2025. According to her message, which was reviewed by ESPN, Herndon wrote that "there is a federal investigation surrounding a man pretending to be a 49ers player," naming Love, and saying he stole money from women and that "he is severely damaging the reputation of your team."

"I wanted you to be aware of the situation and hopefully proactive in denouncing his involvement on your team," she wrote in the message.

In the email exchange provided by Herndon, she received a response from a general Levi's Stadium guest services account a week later on Dec. 27, 2025.

"We take reports of individuals misrepresenting themselves as members of the San Francisco 49ers very seriously," the response said. "For safety and legal reasons, the team cannot comment on ongoing investigations or specific individuals. However, we appreciate you bringing this to our attention and encouraging proactive measures to protect the integrity of the organization.

"If you have information that could assist law enforcement or legal authorities, we encourage you to contact the appropriate agencies directly. Our internal team will also monitor any instances of impersonation and take action as appropriate to protect fans and the team's reputation. Thank you again for your vigilance and concern for the Niners community," the email said.

Herndon said she had no further contact with the 49ers after the email response in December. It's unclear whether anyone at the Niners reviewed the email Herndon said she sent. A Niners team source told ESPN last week that the team had not received any reports about Love before it was contacted by the FBI in August.

On Tuesday, a 49ers spokesperson declined to confirm the email's existence or to provide further comment on the email, citing the FBI's ongoing investigation.

Love and his alleged partner in the scheme, Taylor Chan, were arrested Aug. 24 and charged with wire fraud and conspiracy to commit wire fraud. Federal authorities said the duo defrauded more than two dozen women out of about $1.3 million.

Love would meet women via dating apps, falsely portray himself as a "legitimately wealthy" 49ers player or real estate investor and solicit money from them, the FBI said. According to federal court filings, Love was wearing 49ers apparel when he was arrested in Boise, Idaho, and "the FBI later learned from interviews that Love was in Boise as part of his scheme and was actively defrauding three more victims in Idaho."
